extracted.intended_audience: researchers, educators, and practitioners designing or studying peer assessment and peer grading systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating reviewer-assignment strategies and the number of reviews per submission in peer assessment to optimize grading accuracy, fairness, timeliness, and educational outcomes. This is a systematic literature review synthesizing empirical and qualitative evidence (2010--2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-assignment strategies (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four common reviewer-assignment strategies were identified: random assignment, competency-based assignment, social-network-based assignment, and bidding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four strategies are the primary modes considered in the literature; choice among them affects downstream outcomes (accuracy, fairness, timeliness, educational value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Random assignment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While common, random assignment often results in inconsistent grading and fairness concerns. Use with caution if fairness or consistency are priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency-based assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Competency-based strategies match reviewers to tasks based on demonstrated ability or competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competency-based strategies can address issues of inconsistent grading and improve fairness/accuracy by assigning reviewers with appropriate skill levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social-network-based assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment informed by social network structure (e.g., relationships among students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social-network-based methods have the potential to improve fairness and timeliness, but existing empirical evidence is limited; they are promising but under-studied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding-based assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers bid on submissions they prefer to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidding can potentially improve fairness and timeliness by aligning reviewer interest with assignments; however, empirical evidence supporting its benefits is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviews per submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantity of reviews assigned per artifact/submission (review count).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning three reviews per submission emerges as the most common practice. A range of three to five reviews per student or per submission is frequently cited as a recommended spot that balances grading accuracy, student workload, learning outcomes, and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which peer grades reflect correct/consistent evaluations of submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both reviewer-assignment strategy and the number of reviews affect accuracy; competency-based assignment and increasing reviewer count (to a point) can improve accuracy, but trade-offs with workload exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness of grading
rubrics_metrics.description: Equity and consistency in how submissions are assessed across students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random assignment can lead to fairness concerns; competency-based, social-network-based, and bidding approaches are discussed as ways to mitigate fairness issues, subject to empirical validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational value / learning outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which peer assessment produces timely, high-quality feedback that enhances student learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices (assignment strategy and review count) should consider impacts on learning outcomes; the literature recommends balancing review count to support learning while managing workload and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of grading
rubrics_metrics.description: How quickly peer feedback is delivered to students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social-network-based and bidding methods may improve timeliness, but evidence is limited. Timeliness is a trade-off to consider alongside accuracy and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student workload
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of work required from students to perform peer reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workload is a key balancing factor when choosing review count (more reviews can improve accuracy but increase workload); recommended review counts (3--5) aim to balance workload with other goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of student participation and investment in the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement interacts with assignment strategy and review count; selecting methods and counts that maintain engagement is part of optimizing peer assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-offs among outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The need to weigh competing goals (accuracy, fairness, timeliness, workload, learning outcomes, engagement) when selecting assignment strategies and review counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical decisions should consider trade-offs: e.g., increasing reviewer count may improve accuracy but raise workload; competency-based assignment may improve fairness but require additional information about reviewer competence; empirical evidence is uneven across strategies.
